coordinates.locator: Nominatim result for 'Laboratoire Souterrain a Bas Bruit Rustrel' (OpenStreetMap way 130547816, 'Galerie A')
coordinates.note: Approximate, campus-grade: the OpenStreetMap position of the laboratory ('Galerie A', Rustrel), probably the entrance area on the surface; the underground galleries (about 3.2 km of galleries in the 1999 paper, down to about 500 m depth) are not located by it. No official LSBB page and no paper read gives a latitude and longitude. The official address is '279 Chemin de la Grande Combe, 84400 Rustrel' (lsbb.eu).

depth_mwe.note: The 1999 characterisation paper says 'about 1,500 m.w.e.' for the capsule and surrounding rooms.
depth_mwe.quote: At 1500 mwe, the ambient neutron flux

depth_rock.note: The official history page says the fire-control post was buried 'à plus de 500 mètres de profondeur'; the SIMPLE paper (arXiv:1404.4309) puts the GESA cavern at 505 m.
depth_rock.quote: The deepest experimental hall (500 m of calcite rock overburden)

name: Laboratoire Souterrain à Bas Bruit (Rustrel)
notes: A17: the coordinate rests on a geocoder (rank 8), so it is a campus-grade point marked approximate; it is not relabelled as a detector or underground-lab position.

summary.plain: The underground laboratory at Rustrel in the Vaucluse, France, under a limestone mountain, about 500 m below the surface.
summary.technical: LSBB galleries under the Grande Montagne of the Plateau d'Albion; deepest hall under 500 m of calcite rock, about 1500 m.w.e. The recorded point is an approximate surface position; the underground galleries extend over kilometres.
